newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish elections on September 21, president says.
newsitem.headline: Polish elections on September 21, president says.

text.p: President Aleksander Kwasniewski, in a televised address on Wednesday, set the date of Poland's parliamentary elections for September 21.

"I want to put Poland's affairs in order, I want to strengthen our democracy -- and this has persuaded me to decide today that the parliamentary elections will take place on September 21," Kwasniewski said on public television.
A source close to the president had told Reuters earlier on Wednesday that Kwasniewski would announce September 14 as the day for the elections.
By law, the elections have to held on a day free of work within a month before the end of parliament's term, which falls on October 14 this year.
Explaining his final choice of date, Kwasniewski told Poles it would let them enjoy summer holidays in peace and still leave time for an election campaign that addressed the issues.

Kwasniewski said he planned to sign the new constitution -- which Poles narrowly approved in a referendum last month -- in mid-July, as the Supreme Court was now still examining various protests against it.
He said the elections should be conducted under laws now in force but the new parliament after the vote should form a government under the rules of the new constitution.

The election, the third free parliamentary vote since the fall of communism in 1989, will pit the ruling former communists against a right-wing opposition bloc gathered around the Solidarity trade union.

With opinion polls showing both the ex-communist Democratic Left Alliance (SLD) and the opposition Solidarity Election Action (AWS) with about 25 percent support each, the balance of power in the next parliament could be held by smaller parties.
Both the AWS and SLD adhere to pro-market policies and support integration with the European Union and NATO.
The Solidarity alliance's platform is oriented more towards religious and patriotic values while the SLD, in power since 1993 elections along with the Peasant Party (PSL), is secular in approach.
